data.title: worker-report lab: design how wf writes and sends reports when a worker is done

data.text:
Goal: the worker-report lab. It designs, end to end, how wf writes and sends a worker's report when the worker is done, so the report lands on the page and Prima can retrieve it on GitHub. Matthew: "Going forward they should be pushing reports to you on Github.  We need a wf space for those to land in pages.  So you can retrieve and see the reports there.  We use github as our nexus for information for now." (t526u). "That needs to be built into wf so when the worker is done, the wf sending the report once it is taught where it should land them." (t527u). "We should get claude to work on this as a lab so we can get it built well. Take all I said above plan it out.  message me when your ready.  So I can see you need me.  We need this before we can setup more workers.  For brief fast messages like we are trouble shooting.  prompt boxes are good.  But for normal wf loops we use packs > returns > review through github with WF controlling it." (t528u). Words: docs/review/DIRECTOR-WORDS-t526-t528u.md. Lab band door: 90.50.10.0700.
Builder: Claude (Matthew's PC, D:\Git\claude). Checker: Grok-Check (wf check --as Grok-Check).
Serves: no page yet. This lab designs the report system and proposes the Grok build pages. Those pages, once packed, write "Lab: 90.50.10.0705" and this lab lists them under Serves.
Why a new lab: no lab on the door tries this subject. 0701 is the wf loop harness, 0702 is seq grammar, 0703 is seq storage, 0704 is drift-check and worker design. This lab is the report system we need before setting up more workers (t528u). 0705 is the next free number after 0704 on this book.
This pack is a frame, not a script. Matthew works with Claude directly. Claude may follow Matthew's direction within the grant labs/0705/, including adding further files under that folder. Research only: no changes to src/, tests/, or any code.
Done when: labs/0705/DESIGN.md designs the worker-report system end to end from t526u, t527u and t528u: wf is taught once where reports land; when a worker finishes (build return, check, setup, lab, troubleshooting), wf writes and pushes the report to GitHub so it lands on the page; Prima retrieves it via GitHub. The file has sections ## 1. through ## 4.
Done when: labs/0705/SPEC.md specifies the run-folder config, the commands (what wf does on return, check, setup, lab, and troubleshooting), the report file format, and how a report is logged in the hash chain. The file has sections ## 1. through ## 4.
Done when: labs/0705/WORKER-SETUP.md says how a new worker is set up so reports work, so we can add more workers, and distinguishes prompt boxes (brief troubleshooting) from the normal loop (packs > returns > review through GitHub, with wf controlling it). The file has sections ## 1. through ## 3.
Done when: labs/0705/FAILURES.md covers at least push rejected, offline, Codex no-network, and a dead lock. The file has sections ## 1. through ## 4.
Done when: labs/0705/BUILD-PAGES.md proposes a split of the build into disjoint-grant pages for Grok builders (the files, the order, and what each page waits on). The file has sections ## 1. through ## 3.
Done when: labs/0705/LESSONS.md is a short list of lessons, each with a file:line or commit cite.

fields.w01: Write labs/0705/DESIGN.md. Design the wf worker-report system end to end from t526u, t527u and t528u. Section "## 1. Goal": what "reports live in pages" means, and that GitHub is the nexus Prima reads. Section "## 2. Loop": the normal loop is packs > returns > review through GitHub, with wf controlling it; prompt boxes are only for brief troubleshooting. Section "## 3. Where reports land": wf is taught once (run-folder config: branch and path). Section "## 4. When wf writes": when a worker finishes a build return, a check, setup, a lab, or troubleshooting, wf writes and pushes the report so it lands on the page.
fields.w02: Write labs/0705/SPEC.md. Section "## 1. Config": the run-folder config (branch, path, and any other field), where the file lives, and who writes it once. Section "## 2. Commands": what wf does on return, check, setup, lab, and troubleshooting, and whether a `wf report` command is also needed. Section "## 3. Report file": path, filename, required fields, and the copy that lives on the page's pass. Section "## 4. Hash chain": the log entry kind and fields, and what later hooks in src/page.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cmd.rs or src/render.rs would be needed.
fields.w03: Write labs/0705/WORKER-SETUP.md. Section "## 1. New worker": the steps to add another worker so reports already work (folder, wf version, run-folder config, name). Section "## 2. Config once": what is configured once per run folder, not per prompt. Section "## 3. Prompt vs pack": when a prompt box is right (brief troubleshooting) and when the normal pack/return/review loop is required.
fields.w04: Write labs/0705/FAILURES.md. Section "## 1. Push rejected": fetch and rebase, never force; what wf must tell the worker. Section "## 2. Offline": what is recorded locally and what is retried. Section "## 3. Codex no-network": Codex CLI may have no git network; how a report still lands, or how the lab says it cannot. Section "## 4. Dead lock": a dead .wf-lock during a report write or push (page 0420 is the later fix; this section says what the report path should do until then).
fields.w05: Write labs/0705/BUILD-PAGES.md. Section "## 1. Split": the proposed Grok build pages, starting at 0422 unless a better number is required, each with a title and outcome. Section "## 2. Grants": the files each page may touch, disjoint from each other and from open pages (0407 src/render.rs, 0408 src/cmd.rs src/lib.rs src/page.rs, 0419 src/git.rs). A new module such as src/report.rs is allowed. Section "## 3. Order": what each page waits on, and that none of them are packed until this lab closes.
fields.w06: Write labs/0705/LESSONS.md, a short list of lessons (what went wrong or what held, why, what to do next time), each with a file:line or commit cite (t506u).

The design keeps the kit rules: the log is the only truth, views are printed, the lock is per page, and there are no force pushes. Five things it found in the code:
  (1) `wf check` never pushes (src/cmd.rs:786-793). That is why checks can stay in one run folder. GROK-BUILDER-QUEUE.md:50 asks checkers to push the log by hand.
  (2) The lock is held through the whole `return --push`, push included (src/lib.rs:154; src/cmd.rs:533-536). A killed push can therefore leave a dead lock.
  (3) intake gives the same refusal for a log that is behind as for one that has diverged (src/cmd.rs:629-631). 0702 was refused that way on 2026-11-23.
  (4) The stopgap rebases on a rejected push (REPORTS.md:68-72), while wf merges (src/cmd.rs:574). The design keeps the merge, so recorded commit SHAs stay on the branch.
  (5) A new src/report.rs cannot compile without `mod report;` in src/lib.rs, which 0408 holds. So report pages 0422-0424 wait on 0408 and on the lib/page/cmd queue (waves 3-10); DESIGN.md 4.1 Q2 asks Matthew whether they go first.
